title: Week in Orbit
summary: The space industry is grappling with rising costs and launch risks while new funding rounds and partnerships continue to reshape the landscape. Notably, the Space Force is under scrutiny for its satellite expenses, and several companies are positioning themselves for upcoming contracts.

themes.title: Cost Concerns in Space Force
themes.body: The GAO has flagged significant cost overruns and launch risks in the Space Force's satellite portfolio, raising questions about budget management. With a proposed $1.4 billion increase to the space resilience line in the FY27 budget, the pressure to deliver value is mounting.

themes.title: Funding Rounds Heat Up
themes.body: Chinese satellite manufacturer Hongqing's recent $191 million raise underscores the competitive capital landscape in space tech. Meanwhile, True Anomaly's $190 million Series C funding round highlights investor appetite for innovative space solutions.

themes.title: Launch Contracts and Partnerships
themes.body: Isar Aerospace's contract with Planet for satellite launches signals a growing trend of European companies entering the commercial space race. Additionally, Anduril and L3Harris are teaming up for a tactical SDA constellation bid, indicating a shift towards collaborative defense initiatives.

themes.title: Emerging Technologies in Space
themes.body: Verde Technologies' pivot to perovskite solar panels for space applications reflects a broader interest in sustainable technologies. As the industry evolves, the integration of AI and advanced materials will likely play a critical role in future missions.
